item.title: 4th Line Lower Attachment
item.description: 4th Line Lower Attachment Meaning The 4th line lower attachment is a contact play where you attach directly underneath an opponent’s high stone on the fourth line, placing your stone on the third line.

item.title: Answer Atari
item.description: Answer atari What it means A stone or group in atari has only one liberty.

item.title: Armpit Hit
item.description: Armpit Hit Meaning The armpit hit is a contact move played directly underneath an opponent’s high stone (typically on the fourth line) on the third line, placed along the side of the stone.

item.title: Arrowhead
item.description: Arrowhead Meaning The arrowhead (or spearhead shape) is an aggressive, triangular formation of stones pointing directly into the opponent’s sphere of influence or through a narrow corridor between enemy stones.

item.title: Bamboo Joint
item.description: bamboo_joint Example Meaning A bamboo joint is a strong, flexible connection made from two parallel pairs of stones with a one-point gap between the pairs.

item.title: Bend
item.description: Bend (Magari) Meaning The bend (magari) is a powerful turn played at the head of a line of stones.

item.title: Big Bend
item.description: Big Bend (Grand Turn) Meaning The big bend is a sweeping, large-scale turn played at the intersection of two major spheres of influence.

item.title: Big Bulge
item.description: Big Bulge (Fukurami) Meaning The big bulge (fukurami) is an expanding shape move where a stone bows outward from a contact fight rather than retreating or connecting flatly.

item.title: Butting Play
item.description: Butting Play (Tsukiatari) Meaning A butting play (tsukiatari) is a direct head-on collision where a stone is played straight into the head of an opposing stone along the same grid line.

item.title: Cap
item.description: Cap What is a cap? A cap is a move played in front of an opposing stone or group, usually one or two lines away.
